## 0. Conventions, scope, and imported inputs

### 0.1 Ground field, coefficients, Hodge theory

All Hodge-theoretic statements are over `k = C` and with `Q`-coefficients; the imported geometry is valid over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and is used here after base change to `C`. For a separated Deligne-Mumford stack `X` of finite type over `C` the groups `H^*(X;Q)`, `H^*_c(X;Q)` and `H^{BM}_*(X;Q)` carry functorial mixed Hodge structures (via a smooth simplicial atlas, or equivalently via the coarse space with `Q`-coefficients), Poincare duality holds when `X` is smooth, and:

* **(W1)** `H^m_c(X;Q)` has weights `<= m`; `H^m(X;Q)` has weights `>= m` when `X` is smooth. (Deligne, Hodge II/III.)
* **(W2)** Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for `W`, so `Gr^W_m` is an exact functor on mixed Hodge structures.
* **(W3)** For an open-closed decomposition `X = V sqcup Y` (with `V` open, `Y` closed) there is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures `... -> H^{m-1}_c(Y) -> H^m_c(V) -> H^m_c(X) -> H^m_c(Y) -> ...`.
* **(W4)** `H^{BM}_m(X;Q)` is dual to `H^m_c(X;Q)` in the same degree with no extra Tate twist; the dual of `Q(-8)` is `Q(8)`. (Working-context established fact.)

Accordingly, for every `X` and `m` set

> `T_m(X) := W_{-m} H^{BM}_m(X;Q)`, so that `T_m(X)` is canonically dual to `Gr^W_m H^m_c(X;Q)`.

By (W1), `T_m(X)` is the **lowest**-weight graded piece of `H^{BM}_m(X;Q)`, and `Gr^W_m H^m_c(X;Q)` is the **top**-weight graded piece of `H^m_c(X;Q)` in its own degree, i.e. the corner `weight = degree`.

### 0.2 The exact target and the object of this subproblem

The exact campaign target is `W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21)`, asserted to be a direct sum of `Q(8)` (FND-0001; pinned arithmetic `d = 3*6-3+6 = 21`, `2d-16 = 26`, `Q(-13)(21) = Q(8)`). In the notation above the target is `T_16(M_{6,6})`.

The object of C66-TATE-SUPPORT is the contribution of the balanced tetragonal Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure model `Z`. This artifact takes the *exact codimension-thirteen contribution supported on Z* to be the group

> `T_16(Z) = W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Z;Q)`, dual to `Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(Z;Q)`,

and the demanded Tate type to be `T_16(Z) = ` a direct sum of `Q(8)`, equivalently `Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(Z;Q) = ` a direct sum of `Q(-8)`. This reading is forced by weight bookkeeping: whatever morphism `Z -> M_{6,6}` C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY eventually constructs, the induced map on `H^{BM}_{16}` is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, so by strictness (W2) the weight `-16` part of its image is the image of `T_16(Z)`; Tate type of `T_16(Z)` is therefore exactly what the assembly node needs from this node.

**What is deliberately not claimed here.** No morphism `Z -> M_{6,6}` is constructed (FND-0137, FND-0098); no closedness, purity, codimension, Gysin map or `Aut(C,Gamma)` clause is asserted (FND-0052); and it is *not* claimed that the balanced reduced-support model exhausts the closed evaluation-failure locus in `M_{6,6}` (archive constraint: unbalanced splitting types, non-reduced divisors and jumping strata remain in the closed locus). Those are C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY obligations.

## 1. The weight-truncation lemma

**Lemma 1.1.** Let `X` be a separated Deligne-Mumford stack of finite type over `C`, let `j : V -> X` be an open immersion and `Y := X minus V` the complementary closed substack with its reduced structure. Then for every `m` the map

`Gr^W_m H^m_c(V;Q) --> Gr^W_m H^m_c(X;Q)`

is **injective**. Dually, `T_m(X) -> T_m(V)` is **surjective**.

*Proof.* By (W3) the sequence of mixed Hodge structures

`H^{m-1}_c(Y;Q) --> H^m_c(V;Q) --> H^m_c(X;Q)`

is exact. By (W1) all weights on `H^{m-1}_c(Y;Q)` are `<= m-1`, hence `Gr^W_m H^{m-1}_c(Y;Q) = 0`. By (W2) the functor `Gr^W_m` is exact, so applying it gives an exact sequence `0 -> Gr^W_m H^m_c(V) -> Gr^W_m H^m_c(X)`, which is the assertion. The dual statement follows from (W4) and exactness of `Q`-linear duality. `QED`

**Remark 1.2 (why this is the right corner, and how the archive constraint is respected).** The working context records as a hard constraint: *removing the discriminant from a `P^2`-bundle leaves only the projective-bundle cohomology relevant to the lowest-weight calculation*, with the reason that the discriminant complement has additional cohomology and monodromy. Lemma 1.1 does **not** assert that. It asserts a strictly one-sided injection in the single corner `weight = degree`, and it proves it. The additional classes of the complement are precisely the image of the connecting map from `H^{m-1}_c(Y)`; the constraint is right that they exist and are not controlled, and the lemma shows only that they carry weights `<= m-1` and therefore cannot occupy `Gr^W_m`. No claim is made about `H^m_c(V)` as a whole, about its monodromy, or about any graded piece of weight `< m`. Note also that the degree drop `m -> m-1` is a *degree* phenomenon, not a statement about the weights of a coefficient object; this is what keeps the argument outside the scope of FND-0164 (Section 5).

**Remark 1.3.** Lemma 1.1 is exactly the reason the exact target is attackable at all in this lane: the demanded group `T_16` is the lowest-weight graded piece of Borel-Moore homology, and by Lemma 1.1 it can only *shrink* when one passes from a compactification-in-the-large to an open piece. The whole of Sections 3-4 consists of choosing ambients in which the corner is computed by constant Tate coefficients.

## 2. The balanced model; the discriminant is an ample relative divisor

### 2.1 Setup

**Definition 2.1.** Let `S` be a reduced locally Noetherian `C`-scheme carrying a genus-six degree-four family `gamma : script-C -> P` with `P -> S` a `P^1`-bundle, satisfying `(CE)`, `(N)` and `(BAL)` and the standing hypotheses of ATT-0112 clause (E). Write:

* `pi : script-C -> S` the universal curve: smooth and proper, geometrically connected fibres of genus six, relative dimension one;
* `L := W_5 tensor omega_{script-C/S}^{-1}`, of fibre degree `6` (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6; global existence and base-invisibility of the residual twist: FND-0157). By ATT-0086/CLM-0086-1, CLM-0086-2 and FND-0139 (imported through ATT-0112), `h^0(L_s) = 3` on **every** geometric fibre, with no jumping; by FND-0130 and FND-0134, `L_s` is base-point-free;
* `A := P_S(pi_*L) -> S`: by ATT-0088/CLM-0088-8 and FND-0157, `pi_*L` is locally free of rank three over the reduced base `S`, compatibly with base change, and `A` is a **Zariski-locally trivial `P^2`-bundle**, proper and smooth over `S` of pure relative dimension two. By ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 this is the relative Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure incidence;
* `script-D subset script-C x_S A`: the universal degree-six divisor, a relative effective Cartier divisor, finite flat of degree six over `A` (write `q : script-D -> A`);
* `Delta subset A`: the locus of non-reduced divisors, with `U := A minus Delta` the reduced-support open. `U` is nonempty and dense in every fibre by FND-0134;
* `Z := Ord(U) -> U`: the finite etale right `S_6`-torsor of orderings, of degree `720` (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8; ATT-0066/CLM-0066-6). `Z` is `S`-smooth of pure relative dimension two (FND-0141).

In the load-bearing application `S` is a connected component of a smooth atlas of `Hbar^bal`, so `dim S = 15` (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7) and `dim A = dim U = dim Z = 17`. The numerical codimension `21 - 17 = 4` in `M_{6,6}` is recorded only as orientation; **no** dimension enters the weight arguments of Sections 3-4.

### 2.2 `Delta` is a relatively ample effective Cartier divisor

**Lemma 2.2.** `Delta` is the zero scheme of the discriminant section

`disc in Gamma(A, (det q_* O_{script-D})^{tensor -2})`

of the rank-six `O_A`-algebra `q_*O_{script-D}`. It is an effective Cartier divisor on `A` whose restriction to every geometric fibre `A_b = |L_b| = P^2` is a **nonzero** effective divisor, i.e. a plane curve of some degree `d >= 1` (`d` locally constant on `S`). Consequently:

1. `Delta` is relatively ample over `S`, and `U = A minus Delta -> S` is an **affine** morphism;
2. `Z -> S` is an affine morphism;
3. every geometric fibre `U_b` and `Z_b` is a **smooth affine surface**.

*Proof.* (a) `q` is finite flat of degree six, being the projection of a relative effective Cartier divisor of degree six inside a smooth curve fibration; hence `script-A := q_*O_{script-D}` is a locally free `O_A`-algebra of rank six. The discriminant of a finite locally free algebra is a canonical global section of `(det script-A)^{tensor -2}` whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change, and (characteristic zero, so ramification is tame) its vanishing locus is exactly the non-etale locus of `q`, i.e. the locus of points of `A` over which the fibre of `q` is non-reduced. That locus is `Delta`. Being the zero scheme of a section of a line bundle, `Delta` is an effective Cartier divisor once the section is not a zero divisor, which follows from (b).

(b) `disc` does not vanish identically on any fibre `A_b`: by FND-0134 the general member of `|L_b|` consists of six distinct points, so `Delta_b` is a proper closed subset of `A_b = P^2`. Hence `disc|_{A_b}` is a nonzero section of `O_{P^2}(d)` for some `d >= 0`, and `Delta_b` is an effective plane divisor of degree `d`, in particular of pure dimension one when `d >= 1`.

(c) `Delta_b` is nonempty: by FND-0136, for every `p in C_b` one has `h^0(L_b(-2p)) >= 1`, so `|L_b|` contains a divisor non-reduced at `p`. Hence `d >= 1`.

(d) Therefore `O_A(Delta)` restricts on each fibre to `O_{P^2}(d)` with `d >= 1`, which is ample; so `Delta` is a relatively ample effective Cartier divisor on the proper `S`-scheme `A`. The complement of a relatively ample effective divisor in a scheme proper over `S` is affine over `S`, giving (1). `Z -> U` is finite, hence affine, and a composition of affine morphisms is affine, giving (2). For (3): `U_b = P^2 minus Delta_b` is the complement of an ample divisor in a projective variety, hence affine, and smooth as an open in `P^2`; `Z_b -> U_b` is finite (so `Z_b` is affine) and etale (so `Z_b` is smooth). `QED`

**Remark 2.3 (the affineness constraint is respected).** The archive records as blocked: *an open subset of an affine stack is automatically affine, so its cohomology vanishes above the dimension of the ambient affine stack*. Lemma 2.2 never uses that inference. Affineness of `U_b` comes from Serre's criterion applied to the **ample divisor that is removed**; affineness of `Z_b` from finiteness of `Z_b -> U_b`. Moreover **no affineness, quasi-affineness or cohomological-dimension statement about the base `S` is asserted or used anywhere in this artifact**, and none is needed: Sections 3-4 use only Lemma 1.1 and the projective-bundle formula.

### 2.3 Fibrewise vanishing

**Corollary 2.4.** For every geometric point `b` of `S`: `H^q(U_b;Q) = H^q(Z_b;Q) = 0` for `q > 2` (Artin-Grothendieck vanishing on an affine variety of dimension two), hence by Poincare duality on the smooth surfaces `U_b`, `Z_b`, `H^q_c(U_b;Q) = H^q_c(Z_b;Q) = 0` for `q < 2`. Consequently, with `g : Z -> S`, proper base change for `Rg_!` identifies the stalk of `R^q g_! Q_Z` at a geometric point `s` with `H^q_c(Z_s;Q)`, so

`R^q g_! Q_Z = 0` for `q in {0,1}` and for `q > 4`.

(The last vanishing because the fibres have dimension two.) A constructible complex all of whose stalks vanish is zero, so these are genuine sheaf vanishings.

**Proposition 2.5 (fibrewise top-weight corner of the unordered fibre; NOT used in Theorem A).** For every geometric point `b`,

`Gr^W_q H^q_c(U_b;Q) = 0` for `0 <= q <= 3`, and `Gr^W_4 H^4_c(U_b;Q) = Q(-2)`.

*Proof.* Apply (W3) to `A_b = U_b sqcup Delta_b` with `A_b = P^2` and `Delta_b` proper:

`H^{q-1}(Delta_b) -> H^q_c(U_b) -> H^q(P^2) -> H^q(Delta_b)`.

Apply `Gr^W_q`; the first term dies because `Delta_b` is proper, so `H^{q-1}(Delta_b)` has weights `<= q-1`. Hence `Gr^W_q H^q_c(U_b) = ker(H^q(P^2) -> Gr^W_q H^q(Delta_b))`, and since `H^q(P^2)` is pure of weight `q` its image in `H^q(Delta_b)` is pure of weight `q` and meets `W_{q-1}` trivially, so this kernel equals `ker(H^q(P^2) -> H^q(Delta_b))`. Now: for `q = 1,3`, `H^q(P^2) = 0`. For `q = 0`, `H^0(P^2) = Q -> H^0(Delta_b)` is injective because `Delta_b` is nonempty (Lemma 2.2(c)). For `q = 2`: by Lemma 2.2, `Delta_b` is an effective plane divisor, so all its irreducible components `Delta_1, ..., Delta_r` have dimension one; for a proper reduced curve, `H^2(Delta_b;Q) = H^2` of its normalization `= Q(-1)^r`, and the hyperplane class `h` restricts on the normalization of `Delta_i` to `deg(Delta_i) != 0` times the point class, so `H^2(P^2) = Q(-1)h -> H^2(Delta_b)` is injective and the kernel is `0`. For `q = 4`: `H^4(Delta_b) = 0` since `dim Delta_b = 1`, so the kernel is all of `H^4(P^2) = Q(-2)`. `QED`

**Remark 2.6 (explicitly non-load-bearing).** Proposition 2.5 is recorded because it identifies, fibrewise, *which* Leray row can carry the corner, and it is a correct computation. It is **not** used in the proof of Theorem A, and in particular it is **not** converted into a statement that the coefficient object `R^q f_! Q` has weights `<= q-1` for `q <= 3`. Pointwise weight bounds on the stalks of a mixed Hodge module do not bound the weight of the module, and FND-0164 records precisely that the resulting `Gr^W_{p+q} E_2^{p,q}` is not killed for non-constant coefficients. See Section 5.

## 3. Two ambient bundles with constant Tate coefficients

### 3.1 Level 0: the Abel-Jacobi `P^2`-bundle

By Definition 2.1, `f : A -> S` is a Zariski-locally trivial `P^2`-bundle. The projective bundle formula in compactly supported cohomology is an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures

`H^m_c(A;Q) = H^m_c(S;Q) (+) H^{m-2}_c(S;Q)(-1) (+) H^{m-4}_c(S;Q)(-2)`,

realized by cup product with `1, xi, xi^2` for `xi = c_1(O_A(1))`; it is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures because `xi` is an algebraic class of type `(1,1)`, i.e. because the coefficient objects `Q, Q(-1), Q(-2)` are **constant Tate objects**. Taking `Gr^W_{16}` and using that `Gr^W_{16}(H^{m}_c(S)(-i)) = Gr^W_{m}H^m_c(S)(-i)` when `m + 2i = 16`:

> **(3.1)** `Gr^W_{16} H^{16}_c(A;Q) = Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(S;Q) (+) Gr^W_{14}H^{14}_c(S;Q)(-1) (+) Gr^W_{12}H^{12}_c(S;Q)(-2)`.

### 3.2 Level 1: the universal divisor is a `P^1`-bundle over the universal curve

**Lemma 3.1.** Let `Delta_{script-C} subset script-C x_S script-C` be the diagonal and `pr_1, pr_2` the two projections. Then

`script-G := pr_{2*}(pr_1^* L (-Delta_{script-C}))`

is locally free of rank two on `script-C` and compatible with base change, and the universal divisor `script-D`, viewed over `script-C` by `(p, Gamma) |-> p`, is canonically `script-D = P_{script-C}(script-G)`, a **Zariski-locally trivial `P^1`-bundle** over `script-C`.

*Proof.* Fix a geometric point `p` of `script-C` over `b in S`. The fibre of `script-G` at `p` is `H^0(C_b, L_b(-p))`. Since `h^0(L_b) = 3` (FND-0139; ATT-0086/CLM-0086-1, CLM-0086-2 through ATT-0112) and `L_b` is base-point-free (FND-0130, FND-0134), evaluation at `p` is surjective onto the one-dimensional fibre of `L_b`, so `h^0(L_b(-p)) = 2` for **every** `p`. The base `script-C` is smooth over the reduced `S`, hence reduced, so Grauert's theorem applies (respecting FND-0131, which forbids Grauert over nonreduced bases): `script-G` is locally free of rank two and its formation commutes with base change. The fibre of `script-D -> script-C` over `p` is `{ Gamma in |L_b| : Gamma >= p } = P(H^0(L_b(-p))) = P^1`, and the natural closed immersion `P_{script-C}(script-G) -> script-C x_S A` induced by `script-G -> pr_{2*}pr_1^*L = pi^*pi_*L` identifies `P_{script-C}(script-G)` with `script-D`. The projectivization of a locally free sheaf of rank two is Zariski-locally trivial (it trivializes over any open on which the sheaf is free). A twist of `L` by a line bundle pulled back from `S` changes neither `A` nor `script-D` (FND-0157). `QED`

Hence, again with constant Tate coefficients,

> **(3.2)** `Gr^W_{16} H^{16}_c(script-D;Q) = Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(script-C;Q) (+) Gr^W_{14}H^{14}_c(script-C;Q)(-1)`.

### 3.3 The two open models and their isotypic content

`U subset A` is open by Definition 2.1. Set `Z^{(1)} := script-D|_U = script-D x_A U`, an **open** substack of `script-D` (the preimage of the open `U`). Over `U` the universal divisor is reduced with six distinct points, so `q|_U : Z^{(1)} -> U` is finite etale of degree six.

**Lemma 3.2.** `Z^{(1)} = Z/S_5`, where `S_5 subset S_6` is the stabiliser of the first letter. Consequently, for `Q`-coefficients and every additive `S_6`-equivariant functor `F` to `Q`-vector spaces or mixed `Q`-Hodge structures,

`F(Z^{(1)}) = F(Z)^{S_5} = M_{[6]}(F) (+) M_{[5,1]}(F)`,

where `F(Z) = (+)_rho V_rho tensor M_rho(F)` is the `S_6`-isotypic decomposition and `[6]`, `[5,1]` denote the trivial and standard representations. Moreover `F(Z)^{S_6} = F(U) = M_{[6]}(F)`.

*Proof.* A point of `Z` over `U` is a triple `(b, Gamma, (p_1,...,p_6))` with `Gamma in U_b` and `(p_i)` an ordering of its six distinct support points; quotienting by the free action of `S_5` permuting `p_2, ..., p_6` returns `(b, Gamma, p_1)`, i.e. a point of the universal divisor over `U`. So `Z/S_5 = Z^{(1)}`. With `Q`-coefficients, `F` of a quotient by a finite group is the invariants, so `F(Z^{(1)}) = F(Z)^{S_5}`. Finally `dim V_rho^{S_5} = <Res_{S_5}V_rho, triv> = <V_rho, Ind_{S_5}^{S_6} triv> = ` multiplicity of `rho` in the permutation module `Q[S_6/S_5] = Q^6 = [6] (+) [5,1]`, which is `1` for `rho in {[6],[5,1]}` and `0` otherwise. The last sentence is ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 (with `H_beta = S_6`, the induction functor is the identity), or directly the invariants formula for a finite etale `S_6`-torsor with `Q`-coefficients. `QED`

## 4. Proof of the Theorem

**(A)** is Lemma 1.1.

**(B)** is Lemma 2.2 together with Corollary 2.4.

**(C)** `U` is open in `A`, so Lemma 1.1 gives an injection `Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(U;Q) -> Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(A;Q)`, and (3.1) identifies the target. By Lemma 3.2, `Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(U;Q) = Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(Z;Q)^{S_6}` (taking `S_6`-invariants is exact on `Q`-vector spaces and commutes with `Gr^W`, since `W` is `S_6`-stable). Dualizing with (W4) gives the Borel-Moore form. All four groups are pure polarizable of weight `16`, being graded pieces of mixed Hodge structures in the corner `weight = degree`.

**(D)** The bundle statement is Lemma 3.1 and the identification `Z^{(1)} = Z/S_5` with its isotypic content is Lemma 3.2. `Z^{(1)}` is open in `script-D`, so Lemma 1.1 gives an injection `Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(Z^{(1)};Q) -> Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(script-D;Q)`, and (3.2) identifies the target.

**(E)** Assume **(H-C)**. Then the right-hand side of (D) is `(+) Q(-8) (+) ((+)Q(-7))(-1) = (+) Q(-8)`, a finite direct sum of `Q(-8)`, pure polarizable of weight `16`. By FND-0033 (semisimplicity of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight) every sub-object of such a sum is again a finite direct sum of `Q(-8)`. Q_Z` is `Q(-2)` on the type-(i) open and of higher rank on the type-(ii) locus. Nothing in Sections 3-4 uses this: the arguments there never pass through the fibres of `g`. ## 5. Relation to FND-0164 (the governing adjudicated obstruction)

FND-0164 (corroborated; scope C66-TATE-SUPPORT; recording the failure of ATT-0113/CLM-0113-5) states: in a compact-support Leray spectral sequence `E_2^{p,q} = H^p_c(B; R^q f_! Q)` of mixed Hodge structures, the estimate `weights <= p+q` **does not** kill `Gr^W_{p+q}`; vanishing of `Gr^W_p H^p_c(B;Q)` - including vanishing obtained by compact-support localization of `B` as a dense open in a smooth affine `d`-fold when `p < d` - does not transfer to `Gr^W_{p+w}H^p_c(B;V)` unless `V` is a constant mixed Hodge structure, in particular a constant Tate twist `Q(-m)`; and this applies exactly to the affine relative-dimension-two morphism `f : U -> X^bal` in total degree `p+q = 16` with `p <= 14`. It records one **exception**: *if `R^q f_! Q` is a constant Tate object, the identification `H^p_c(B;Q(-m)) = H^p_c(B;Q)(-m)` does transfer the constant-coefficient top-weight vanishing.*

This artifact respects FND-0164 in the strongest possible way: **clauses (C) and (D) use no Leray spectral sequence at all.** Their two ingredients are

1. Lemma 1.1, whose only weight input is `weights(H^{m-1}_c) <= m-1` on the **same** space - a drop in *cohomological degree*, not a claim about the weight of any coefficient object; and
2. the projective bundle formulas (3.1) and (3.2), whose coefficient objects are `Q`, `Q(-1)`, `Q(-2)` - **constant Tate objects**, i.e. precisely the exception FND-0164 allows.

Accordingly:

* No step of the form *the coefficient object has weights `<= q-1`, hence `Gr^W_{p+q}E_2^{p,q} = 0`* occurs anywhere. Proposition 2.5 is the fibrewise computation that would tempt one into such a step, and Remark 2.6 explicitly refuses to take it.
* No affineness or cohomological-dimension property of the base is used (Remark 2.3), so the `dual Artin vanishing on the affine ambient` route criticized in FND-0164 is not walked; the affineness proved in Lemma 2.2 is used only on the **fibres**, to obtain the sheaf vanishings of Corollary 2.4, which are stalkwise vanishings and carry no weight content.
* No extension of `R^q f_! Q` across a boundary is required, since no coefficient object is transported anywhere.

The genuinely new content relative to ATT-0113 is therefore: an identification of *which part* of the `Z`-supported input can be moved into the constant-Tate-coefficient regime, and a proof that it is at least the `[6]`- and `[5,1]`-isotypic parts.

**Delivered, unconditionally.**

Q_Z = 0` for `q in {0,1}` and `q > 4` (Lemma 2.2, Corollary 2.4). Two of the five potential Leray rows are eliminated outright.

Since the exact target group W_{-16} H^{BM}_16 is dual to precisely this corner Gr^W_16 H^16_c, removing a closed subset can only lose classes there, never create them. Applying this to U inside the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle A and to the level-one model Z^(1) = Z/S_5 inside the universal divisor script-D - which is shown to be a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle over the universal curve script-C, using base-point-freeness of L and h^0(L) = 3 - and then using the projective-bundle formula (whose coefficients are constant Tate objects) gives two unconditional injections of pure weight-sixteen Hodge structures: the S_6-invariant part of Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z) into Gr^W_16 H^16_c(S) + Gr^W_14 H^14_c(S)(-1) + Gr^W_12 H^12_c(S)(-2), and the ([6] + [5,1])-isotypic part into Gr^W_16 H^16_c(script-C) + Gr^W_14 H^14_c(script-C)(-1). Semisimplicity of pure polarizable Hodge structures (FND-0033) then turns Tate-ness of those constant-coefficient corner groups into an honest isomorphism onto a direct sum of Q(8) for the corresponding part of the codimension-thirteen Z-supported input. Independently, the non-reduced-divisor locus Delta inside A is identified as the zero scheme of the discriminant of the degree-six universal divisor, hence a relatively ample effective Cartier divisor: this makes U -> S and Z -> S affine morphisms with smooth affine surface fibres, yields fibrewise Artin vanishing, and gives R^q g_! Q_Z = 0 for q in {0,1} and q > 4. A fibrewise computation records Gr^W_q H^q_c(U_b) = 0 for q <= 3 and = Q(-2) for q = 4; it is deliberately not converted into a weight statement about R^q f_! Q, since that conversion is exactly what FND-0164 forbids. The residual obligation is stated exactly: the isotypic components outside {[6],[5,1]}, and Tate-ness of top-weight compact-support cohomology with constant coefficients on the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz base and its universal curve in degrees 12, 14, 16. No finite computation, no vcd argument, no graph complex, no forgetful map, and no M_{6,6} statement is used.
theorem_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients; for a separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack X over C write T_m(X) := W_{-m} H^{BM}_m(X;Q), so that T_m(X) is canonically dual to Gr^W_m H^m_c(X;Q) with no extra Tate twist, and the Tate type demanded by the exact target at (g,n)=(6,6), m=16 is T_16 = a direct sum of Q(8), equivalently Gr^W_16 H^16_c = a direct sum of Q(-8). Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian C-scheme (in the load-bearing application: a connected component of a smooth atlas of the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz stack Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], which is smooth of pure dimension 15 by ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7) carrying a genus-six degree-four family gamma : script-C -> P with P -> S a P^1-bundle, satisfying (CE)+(N)+(BAL) and the standing hypotheses of ATT-0112 clause (E). Let pi : script-C -> S be the universal curve (smooth proper, relative dimension 1); let L := W_5 tensor omega^{-1} be the CE residual bundle of fibre degree six, so that h^0(L_s) = 3 identically (ATT-0086/CLM-0086-1, CLM-0086-2 and FND-0139, imported through ATT-0112) and L_s is base-point-free (FND-0130, FND-0134); let A := P_S(pi_*L) -> S be the resulting Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle (ATT-0088/CLM-0088-8 via ATT-0112, with FND-0157 for the P^1-bundle target and for base-invisibility of a residual twist of L), which by ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 is the relative Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure incidence; let script-D subset script-C x_S A be the universal degree-six divisor, finite flat of degree six over A; let Delta subset A be the non-reduced-divisor locus, U := A minus Delta the reduced-support open, Z := Ord(U) -> U the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings of degree 720 (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8), and Z^(1) := script-D|_U. Over the 15-dimensional base, dim A = dim U = dim Z = 17. THEN: (A) WEIGHT TRUNCATION. For every open immersion V -> X of separated finite-type DM stacks over C and every m, Gr^W_m H^m_c(V;Q) -> Gr^W_m H^m_c(X;Q) is injective; dually T_m(X) -> T_m(V) is surjective. (B) AFFINENESS. Delta is the zero scheme of the discriminant of the rank-six algebra of script-D over A, hence an effective Cartier divisor on A whose restriction to every geometric fibre A_b = |L_b| = P^2 is a nonzero effective plane divisor; therefore Delta is relatively ample over S, U -> S and Z -> S are affine morphisms, every geometric fibre U_b and Z_b is a smooth affine surface, H^q(U_b;Q) = H^q(Z_b;Q) = 0 for q > 2 and H^q_c(U_b;Q) = H^q_c(Z_b;Q) = 0 for q < 2, and consequently R^q g_! Q_Z = 0 for q in {0,1} and for q > 4, where g : Z -> S. (C) LEVEL-0 REDUCTION (unconditional, constant Tate coefficients). There is an injection of pure polarizable Q-Hodge structures of weight sixteen Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z;Q)^{S_6} = Gr^W_16 H^16_c(U;Q) -> Gr^W_16 H^16_c(S;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H^14_c(S;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H^12_c(S;Q)(-2); dually T_16(U) is a quotient MHS of T_16(S) direct-sum T_14(S)(1) direct-sum T_12(S)(2). (D) LEVEL-1 REDUCTION (unconditional, constant Tate coefficients). script-D is a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle over script-C, namely script-D = P_{script-C}(script-G) with script-G := pr_{2*}(pr_1^* L(-Delta_{script-C})) locally free of rank two; Z^(1) is open in script-D, is finite etale of degree six over U, and equals Z/S_5 for S_5 the stabiliser of the first letter, so that Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z^(1);Q) = Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z;Q)^{S_5} is exactly the sum of the trivial and standard ([6] and [5,1]) S_6-isotypic components of Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z;Q); and there is an injection of pure polarizable Q-Hodge structures of weight sixteen Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z^(1);Q) -> Gr^W_16 H^16_c(script-C;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H^14_c(script-C;Q)(-1). (E) WEAKEST SUFFICIENT CRITERION. Assume (H-C): Gr^W_16 H^16_c(script-C;Q) is a direct sum of Q(-8) and Gr^W_14 H^14_c(script-C;Q) is a direct sum of Q(-7). Then the trivial and standard isotypic components of the exact codimension-thirteen Z-supported input T_16(Z) = W_{-16} H^{BM}_16(Z;Q) are direct sums of Q(8). Assume instead only (H-S): Gr^W_{2j} H^{2j}_c(S;Q) is a direct sum of Q(-j) for j in {6,7,8}. Then the S_6-invariant part of T_16(Z), equivalently T_16(U), is a direct sum of Q(8). Both hypotheses are statements about the corner weight = degree of compactly supported cohomology with CONSTANT Q-coefficients, in the three explicit degrees 12, 14, 16, on the fifteen-dimensional balanced tetragonal Hurwitz base and on its sixteen-dimensional universal curve; no local system, no non-constant coefficient object, and no cohomology of any M_{g,n} occurs in them. (F) NOT ASSERTED. Nothing is claimed about the S_6-isotypic components of Gr^W_16 H^16_c(Z;Q) outside {[6],[5,1]}; no vanishing of any Gr^W_{p+q} E_2^{p,q} with non-constant coefficient object is claimed (FND-0164 stands); no affineness or cohomological-dimension statement about S is used or asserted; and no statement whatever is made about M_{6,6}: no morphism Z -> M_{6,6}, no closedness, purity, Gysin map, codimension, Aut(C,Gamma) or inertia clause, and no claim that the balanced model exhausts the closed evaluation-failure locus.
